grammar.title: To Be: Talking about Origin
grammar.explain_en: We use 'to be' (am, is, are) with 'from' to say where someone or something comes from. We use 'to be' directly with a nationality to say what nationality someone is.
grammar.explain_vi: Chúng ta dùng động từ 'to be' (am, is, are) với 'from' để nói ai đó hoặc vật gì đó đến từ đâu. Chúng ta dùng 'to be' trực tiếp với quốc tịch để nói ai đó thuộc quốc tịch nào.
examples: I am from Vietnam. I am Vietnamese.
He is from Japan. He is Japanese.
They are from America. They are American.
grammar.right: ✅ She is from China. She is Chinese.
grammar.wrong: ❌ She is China. She is from Chinese.

grammar.title: Asking about Countries and Nationalities
grammar.explain_en: Use 'Where' to ask about a country and 'What nationality' to ask about someone's nationality.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng 'Where' (ở đâu) để hỏi về quốc gia và 'What nationality' (quốc tịch gì) để hỏi về quốc tịch của ai đó.
examples: Where are you from? I'm from Vietnam.
What nationality are you? I'm Vietnamese.
Where is she from? She's from England. What nationality is she? She's English.

grammar.title: Capital Letters for Countries and Nationalities
grammar.explain_en: Always use a capital letter for the names of countries and nationalities.
grammar.explain_vi: Luôn luôn viết hoa chữ cái đầu tiên của tên các quốc gia và quốc tịch.
examples: England, English; Japan, Japanese; France, French.
grammar.right: ✅ He is from China. He is Chinese.
grammar.wrong: ❌ He is from china. He is chinese.

grammar.title: Can for Languages
grammar.explain_en: We use 'can' to talk about the ability to speak a language.
grammar.explain_vi: Chúng ta dùng 'can' để nói về khả năng nói một ngôn ngữ nào đó.
examples: She can speak English and French.

readings.title: My New Friend, Ben
readings.text:
My name is Linh. I am nine years old. I am from Vietnam, and I am Vietnamese. I love my country very much. Vietnam is a beautiful country.

Today, I met a new friend. His name is Ben. Ben is also nine years old. He is from America, and he is American. Ben can speak English very well. He is learning Vietnamese, too. Ben likes Vietnamese food, especially phở.

We talked about our countries. Ben showed me a picture of the Statue of Liberty in America. I showed him a picture of Ha Long Bay in Vietnam. We are happy to be friends. We can learn a lot from each other.

readings.title: A Trip Around the World
readings.text:
Minh and Mia are classmates. They love learning about different countries. Last weekend, they visited a special exhibition at the city museum called 'Around the World in One Day'.

First, they stopped at the Japan booth. A friendly Japanese lady showed them how to write their names in Japanese characters. They learned that sushi is a famous Japanese food. Then, they went to the France booth. A French man taught them a few French words like 'Bonjour' and 'Merci'. They saw a model of the Eiffel Tower.

Next, they visited the China booth. They watched a short video about the Great Wall of China and learned that pandas live there. Finally, they came to the Australia booth. An Australian boy, Tom, told them about kangaroos and the beautiful beaches. Minh wants to visit Australia, and Mia dreams of seeing the Eiffel Tower in France. It was a wonderful day!

readings.title: Kids of the World Unite!
readings.text:
Every year, children from all over the world join a special online camp called 'Kids of the World Unite!'. This year, Lucy from England, Hiro from Japan, and An from Vietnam are participating. They meet online every Saturday to share about their lives and countries.

Lucy, who is English, showed them pictures of London, with its famous red buses and Big Ben clock tower. She also taught them a fun English nursery rhyme. Hiro, a Japanese boy, talked about his school in Tokyo and explained how to make origami, a Japanese paper art. He showed them a beautiful paper crane he made. An, who is Vietnamese, proudly presented her country's traditional áo dài and showed a video of a Water Puppet Show, which is very popular in Vietnam.

They discovered many similarities and differences. All three enjoy playing football, but their favorite foods are different: Lucy likes fish and chips, Hiro loves ramen, and An enjoys spring rolls. They also learned about different greetings and customs. They are planning to send each other postcards. This camp helps them understand that even though they live in different corners of the world, they can be great friends and learn to respect each other's cultures. It's truly an amazing way to travel without leaving home!

listening.script: Hello everyone! My name is Ms. Hoa. Today, we are going to talk about different countries and nationalities. Listen carefully! Our first friend is from Japan. She is Japanese. She loves to eat sushi. Our second friend is from America. He is American. He loves to play baseball. Then we have a friend from England. She is English. She likes to drink tea. Next, a friend from France. He is French. He likes to eat croissants. And finally, a friend from China. She is Chinese. She loves pandas. It's wonderful to have friends from all over the world. life_skill.title: BE A GLOBAL CITIZEN
life_skill.intro: Being a global citizen means you understand and respect people from different countries and cultures. You care about the world and try to make it a better place for everyone.
life_skill.intro_vi: Trở thành công dân toàn cầu nghĩa là bạn hiểu và tôn trọng mọi người từ các quốc gia và nền văn hóa khác nhau. Bạn quan tâm đến thế giới và cố gắng biến nó thành một nơi tốt đẹp hơn cho tất cả mọi người.
can_do: Learn about different countries and cultures.
Be kind to people from other countries.
Listen to stories from people around the world.
Try new foods from different countries.
Learn a few words in another language.
Care about global issues, like helping others.

Make friends with people from diverse backgrounds.

fun_facts.en: Did you know? Australia is a country, a continent, and an island all at the same time!

classroom_game.name: Country Guessing Game
steps_en: 1. One student thinks of a country but doesn't say its name.
2. The student gives three clues about the country (e.g., 'It's in Asia. It's famous for sushi. Its flag is white with a red circle.').
3. Other students listen to the clues and guess the country.
4. The first student to guess correctly gets a point. Then, it's their turn to give clues.
steps_vi: 1. Một học sinh nghĩ về một quốc gia nhưng không nói tên.
2. Học sinh đó đưa ra ba gợi ý về quốc gia đó (ví dụ: 'Nó ở châu Á. Nó nổi tiếng với sushi. Cờ của nó màu trắng với một vòng tròn đỏ.').
3. Các học sinh khác lắng nghe gợi ý và đoán tên quốc gia.
4. Học sinh đoán đúng đầu tiên được một điểm. Sau đó, đến lượt họ đưa ra gợi ý.
